title: C. elegans Dissociation for FACS and RNA-seq
author: Robert TP Williams
materials: Prepare reagents in advance L15-10 Buffer: Mix 500 ml Leibovitz's L-15 Medium, 50 ml Fetal Bovine Serum (heat inactivated), 50 ul of 100x Penicillin-Streptomycin solution and 7.7 g sucrose. Filter with 0.2 micron pore filter. Store at 4ºC. Egg Buffer: Mix 29.5 ml of 2M NaCl, 12 ml of 2M KCl, 1 ml of 1M CaCl2, 1 ml of MgCl2, 12.5 ml of 1M HEPES-NaOH pH 7.2 and 435 ml molecular grade water. Filter with 0.2 micron pore filter. Store at 4ºC. Pronase E solution (15 mg/ml): Weigh 150 mg of Protease from Streptomyces griseus (Sigma P8811-1G) into a 15 ml tube. Dissolve the enzyme in 10 ml of Egg Buffer. Nutate the solution for approximately 10 minutes until dissolved. Prepare 1 ml aliquots in 1.5 ml tubes. Store aliquots at -20ºC. SDS-DTT solution: To ensure treatment efficacy, the SDS-DTT solution is prepared fresh on the day of the experiment. Additionally, several aliquots of DTT powder in 1.5 ml tubes are prepared in advance and stored at -20ºC. To prepare the SDS-DTT solution, first resuspend 154 mg of DTT powder with 1 mL of Egg Buffer on the day of the experiment. Then, combine the following reagents in a 15 ml tube (final concentrations in parenthesis): 100 uL of 1M HEPES pH8 (20 mM), 125 uL of 10% SDS (0.25%), 1 mL of 1M DTT (200 mM), 250 uL of 60% sucrose (3%), and 3.525 mL of molecular grade water for a final volume of 5 mL. The SDS-DTT solution is one of the most important reagents to ensure successful dissociation of post-embryonic worms. To check that the SDS-DTT solution is working properly, incubate worms in freshly prepared SDS-DTT solution under a dissection microscope. When prepared properly, worms should dissolve within ~10 minutes of observation.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the workspace and materials for the dissociation process.

substeps.instruction: Cool swinging bucket centrifuge to 4ºC.
Thaw pronase aliquots at room temperature.
Place L15-10 and egg buffer on ice.
Wash and sterilize dounce homogenizer and pestle A using 1ml H20 and 1ml 70% EtOH.

steps.title: Harvest and clean L3 worms
steps.instruction: Isolate synchronized L3 worms and remove contaminating E. coli.

substeps.instruction: Wash plates with fresh M9 to harvest synchronized L3 worms.
Pass the worm suspension through a 20 micron filter to retain L3 stage worms and remove younger worms and E. coli.
Invert the filter and collect retained L3 worms into a fresh 50 ml tube.
Transfer filtered L3 worms to a 15 ml tube.
Pellet worms in a 15 ml tube for 1 min at 2,000 rcf; discard supernatant and repeat M9 washes until supernatant is free of visible E. coli.

steps.title: Initial worm pelleting and sampling
steps.instruction: Concentrate the cleaned worm suspension and set aside a sample for RNA analysis.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge worm suspension at 2,000 rcf for 1 minute.
Resuspend the worm pellet in 1 ml of M9 and transfer to a 1.5 ml tube.
Pellet the worms again at 2000 rcf for 1 minute.
Transfer 10 ul of L1 worm pellet to 1ml of Qiazol and store at -80°C for downstream RNA analysis.

steps.title: SDS-DTT treatment
steps.instruction: Treat worms with SDS-DTT to begin dissociation. Note: If L3 pellet exceeds 200 ul, utilize 2x the L3 pellet volume for chemical/enzymatic treatments.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the worm pellet in 200 ul of fresh SDS-DTT solution.
Incubate for 2 min at room temperature (worms should look ruffled, pharynx should become short and round; do not exceed 2 min).
Quench reaction by adding 800 ul of ice cold egg buffer.
Pellet worms at 13,000 rcf for 15 seconds at 4ºC.
Decant supernatant and replace with 1 ml of ice-cold egg buffer.
Repeat the egg buffer wash for a total of 5 washes.

steps.title: Pronase E digestion and homogenization
steps.instruction: Digest the cuticle and mechanically dissociate the worms.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend SDS-DTT treated worms in 200 ul of 15 mg/ml Pronase E.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature with nutation.
Perform 100 strokes with dounce pestle A to generate a worm slurry.
Visually confirm worm dissociation by viewing a 2 ul sample of worm slurry on a fluorescent microscope.

steps.title: Separate dissociated cells from intact worms
steps.instruction: Use low-speed centrifugation to isolate the cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Pellet undissociated worms at 20 rcf for 1 minute at 4ºC in a swinging bucket centrifuge.
Verify that fluorescent cells are present in the supernatant and absent from the pellet (adjust speed/time if cells are in the pellet).

steps.title: Cell counting and quality control
steps.instruction: Quantify the cell yield and verify cell presence.

substeps.instruction: Load 10 ul of cell suspension onto a Bio-Rad TC20 automated cell counting slide or a hemocytometer.
Microscopically confirm fluorescent cells are present.
If concentration is above 1 x 10^6 cells/ml, dilute the sample to 1 x 10^6 cells/ml using L15-10.
Verify total cell yield is between 2 x 10^6 to 4 x 10^6 cells. If yield is less than 1 x 10^6 cells and many intact worms remain, repeat the SDS-DTT, Pronase E, and dounce homogenization steps.

steps.title: Quench and wash cells
steps.instruction: Stop the enzymatic reaction and wash the cells.

substeps.instruction: Quench Pronase E treatment by adding 1 ml of L15-10.
Pellet the worms at 13,000 rcf for 15 seconds at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend the worms in 1 ml of L15-10.
Pellet the worms at 13,000 rcf for 15 seconds at 4°C.
Resuspend the worms in 1ml of L15-10.

steps.title: Final cell harvest and filtration
steps.instruction: Collect the cell suspension and filter for downstream applications.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 1 ml of the cell-containing supernatant, avoiding the pelleted worm debris.
Dispense the cell suspension through a 35-micron nylon mesh filter into a 5 ml flow cytometry tube.

steps.title: Strain-specific processing
steps.instruction: Perform additional cycles for sorting strains and allocate samples.

substeps.instruction: For the sorting strain, repeat the dissociation and cell harvest (Steps 26-30) for a total of 2-3 homogenization cycles until few intact worms remain.
Final volumes: Control strain = 1ml; Sorting strain = 2-3ml.
Transfer 70 ul of cells to 1 ml of Qiazol and store at -80°C for RNA analysis.
Retain the remaining ~2ml of cells for FACS.
